thread:
maria_support: Hey team — just got an enterprise escalation: customer sees a burst of 502/5xx for streaming responses. They claim client disconnects are being billed as 5xx. Can ops confirm?

ian_ops: Looking at their app logs, client does FIN the socket after ~2s of silence. Our gateway logs show a downstream error around same time, classified as 5xx. Possibly half-close handling mismatch.

jess_support: Customer sent a curl repro: `curl -N -H \"Authorization: Bearer <key>\" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream -d \"{\"prompt\":\"hello\"}\"` then they kill -9 the curl after a few seconds. They say billing showed a 5xx on dashboard.

ian_ops: Can you paste the gateway tail?

maria_support: Paste from their support trace: 
```
2026-03-15T09:12:01Z gateway: incoming request id=abc123
2026-03-15T09:12:03Z proxy: connected to runtime host=rt-23
2026-03-15T09:12:05Z runtime: stream start id=abc123
2026-03-15T09:12:07Z proxy: downstream closed (RST) id=abc123
2026-03-15T09:12:07Z gateway: upstream error 502 code=EPIPE id=abc123
2026-03-15T09:12:07Z billing: mark request as 5xx id=abc123
```

ian_ops: That looks like proxy saw an RST and converted to EPIPE -> gateway returned 502. Our billing pipeline marks any request with response code >=500 as failed for metering reconciliation. So if client-initiated RST is being turned into 5xx, it's double charging.

ryan_devex: This is likely the old NGINX config on the edge + http-proxy behavior. NGINX treats downstream client disconnects as upstream aborts unless half-close is negotiated. We had a followup bug with chunked encoding where a trailing FIN from client arrives while runtime still streaming, producing a SIGPIPE on write.

ian_ops: Repro steps I used locally: start a small server that streams a chunk every 1s, connect with curl `--no-buffer`, kill tcp connection via `sudo tcpkill` at t=3s. Observed proxy log: `writev: broken pipe` then `upstream prematurely closed connection` and gateway returns 502.

maria_support: Customer insists this should be classified as client-abort (4xx) for billing. Is there an existing heuristic?

ian_ops: Heuristic currently: if gateway returns 499 (nginx client closed request) we mark as client-abort and don't count against runtime error budgets. But our gateway returns 502 when proxy detects EPIPE from runtime. So we misclassify client disconnects that race with runtime as 5xx.

sam_billing: That's rough — a number of large accounts have flagged this as billing discrepancies. We need a short repro and a mitigation path. Can we: 1) surface a new metric counting EPIPE-originated 5xx, 2) run a script to reclassify recent spikes where proxy logs show RST/EPIPE?

ian_ops: Agreed. Proposed immediate mitigation: if proxy sees downstream socket close (FIN/RST) within 500ms of upstream write error, tag request as \"client-abort-race\" and exclude from 5xx billing. We'll need a backfill job for the last 30 days.

jess_support: For the customer: request a pcap of the session and the full gateway request ids. Also ask them to try `curl --no-buffer --tcp-nodelay` to reproduce reliably and include `--trace-ascii trace.txt` so we get timing.

ryan_devex: Long-term fix: update gateway to translate upstream EPIPE caused by downstream close into 499 rather than 502 when we can verify the client closed first. Also update proxy to drain KV cache writes after detection instead of aborting with error code.

maria_support: I opened ticket INF-4912 and attached their logs + suggested mitigations. Customer asked for ETA on a rollback/backfill. Ops/Billing needs action items.

sam_billing: Action list from me: 1) Query billing pipeline for all requests flagged 5xx where proxy log contains \"EPIPE\" or \"RST\" in last 14 days. 2) Prepare credit memo script for confirmed client-abort-race entries. 3) Hold refunds until ops confirms root-cause and scope.

ian_ops: Action list from ops: 1) Implement quick heuristic change in proxy (feature flag) to map EPIPE-with-downstream-close -> client-abort tag. 2) Run backfill filter on last 30 days to produce candidate set. 3) Roll to canary tomorrow morning and watch 5xx rate.

maria_support: Customer-facing reply drafted: \"Thanks — we see a race between client disconnect and runtime stream writes. We're tagging those events as client-aborts internally and will reconcile billing where we confirm the race. We'll follow up after internal backfill and canary.\" Please review before I send.

jess_support: LGTM. Include steps they can take to avoid until fix: keepalive pings, or close the stream with server-sent EOF rather than kill -9, or upgrade to our SDK which does graceful half-close.

deploy-bot: Deploy started: proxy/edge canary -> 2026-03-16T02:00:00Z (flag: client-abort-eipemap=true)

ian_ops: Canary looks good so far; 5xx from streaming paths dropped ~72% on canary nodes. Backfill produced ~1.2k candidate events for last 30 days across 14 enterprise customers.

sam_billing: I'll start preparing credit memos for customers with high counts and loop in finance.

maria_support: Great. I'll send the customer the update and the temporary workaround suggestions. Keeping thread open for final reconciliation. :thumbsup:
